# Next.js App Router — URL-Based Screen State

## Principle

Every state that affects what the user sees on screen — active tab, applied filter, sort order, pagination page, selected detail ID, expanded section — should live in the URL query string.

Why:
- The page is shareable (paste a URL → other person sees the same view)
- The browser back/forward button works correctly without extra code
- A refresh restores the same state
- Claude Code (or any tool) can be pointed at a specific UI state by URL
- Deep linking from emails, push notifications, or other apps just works

---

## What goes in the URL

| State | In URL? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Active tab | ✅ Yes | Tab is part of "what is the user looking at" |
| Filter values (search, tag, status) | ✅ Yes | Shareable view |
| Sort column and order | ✅ Yes | Same as filter |
| Pagination page | ✅ Yes | Refreshable list position |
| Selected detail ID (when shown inline) | ✅ Yes | Deep link to specific item |
| Form draft values | ❌ No | User input — too noisy, security-sensitive |
| Loading / error UI state | ❌ No | Transient |
| Animation / expansion state | ❌ No | Purely visual |
| Modal open/close | ⚠️ Sometimes | Yes if the modal should be linkable; otherwise local state |

---

## Implementation — read

```tsx
"use client"

import { useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"

const searchParams = useSearchParams()

const tab    = searchParams.get("tab") ?? "list"
const filter = searchParams.get("filter") ?? ""
const tags   = searchParams.getAll("tag")           // multiple values
const page   = Number(searchParams.get("page") ?? "1")
```

`useSearchParams()` returns a `ReadonlyURLSearchParams`. It re-renders the component when the URL changes (back/forward, programmatic push).

---

## Implementation — write

```tsx
"use client"

import { useRouter, usePathname, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
import { useCallback } from "react"

const router = useRouter()
const pathname = usePathname()
const searchParams = useSearchParams()

/** URL クエリを部分的に更新する */
const updateQuery = useCallback((patch: Record<string, string | string[] | null>) => {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())

  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch)) {
    if (value === null || value === "") {
      params.delete(key)
    } else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
      params.delete(key)
      value.forEach((v) => params.append(key, v))
    } else {
      params.set(key, value)
    }
  }

  router.push(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`)
}, [router, pathname, searchParams])

// Usage
updateQuery({ tab: "settings" })
updateQuery({ filter: null })   // remove
updateQuery({ tag: ["new", "popular"] })  // replace array
```

### `router.push` vs `router.replace`

| Method | Pushes a new history entry | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `router.push` | ✅ Yes | Back button should undo the change (filter change, tab switch) |
| `router.replace` | ❌ No | Quiet state change (debounced search input, derived state) |

Default to `push`. Use `replace` only for high-frequency updates that would clutter history.

---

## Wrap into a state hook

For each screen, encapsulate URL state behind a dedicated hook:

```ts
// _hooks/useResourceListUrlState.ts
"use client"

import { useRouter, usePathname, useSearchParams } from "next/navigation"
import { useCallback, useMemo } from "react"

export const useResourceListUrlState = () => {
  const router = useRouter()
  const pathname = usePathname()
  const searchParams = useSearchParams()

  const state = useMemo(() => ({
    tab:    searchParams.get("tab")   ?? "list",
    filter: searchParams.get("filter") ?? "",
    tags:   searchParams.getAll("tag"),
    page:   Number(searchParams.get("page") ?? "1"),
  }), [searchParams])

  const updateQuery = useCallback((patch: Record<string, string | string[] | null>) => {
    const params = new URLSearchParams(searchParams.toString())
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(patch)) {
      if (value === null || value === "") params.delete(key)
      else if (Array.isArray(value)) {
        params.delete(key); value.forEach((v) => params.append(key, v))
      } else params.set(key, value)
    }
    router.push(`${pathname}?${params.toString()}`)
  }, [router, pathname, searchParams])

  return {
    ...state,
    setTab:    (v: string) => updateQuery({ tab: v, page: "1" }),
    setFilter: (v: string) => updateQuery({ filter: v, page: "1" }),
    setTags:   (v: string[]) => updateQuery({ tag: v, page: "1" }),
    setPage:   (v: number)  => updateQuery({ page: String(v) }),
  }
}
```

The Screen component uses the hook and never touches `useRouter` directly.

---

## Tab integration example

```tsx
const { tab, setTab } = useResourceListUrlState()

<Tabs value={tab} onChange={(v) => setTab(v ?? "list")}>
  <Tabs.List>
    <Tabs.Tab value="list">一覧</Tabs.Tab>
    <Tabs.Tab value="archive">アーカイブ</Tabs.Tab>
  </Tabs.List>
  <Tabs.Panel value="list">...</Tabs.Panel>
  <Tabs.Panel value="archive">...</Tabs.Panel>
</Tabs>
```

The URL becomes `?tab=archive` — bookmarkable, shareable, history-aware.

---

## Side effect: reset pagination on filter change

When a filter changes, page 1 is the only sensible target. Bake this into the setter:

```ts
setFilter: (v: string) => updateQuery({ filter: v, page: "1" }),
setTags:   (v: string[]) => updateQuery({ tag: v, page: "1" }),
```

Pagination changes don't reset filter — they're additive.

---

## Validating URL state

Untrusted URL input must be validated. Use Zod for non-trivial parsing:

```ts
import { z } from "zod"

const UrlStateSchema = z.object({
  tab: z.enum(["list", "archive", "shared"]).default("list"),
  page: z.coerce.number().int().min(1).default(1),
  sortOrder: z.enum(["asc", "desc"]).default("desc"),
})

const raw = Object.fromEntries(searchParams.entries())
const state = UrlStateSchema.parse(raw)
```

This protects against garbage URLs (`?tab=hack`) and gives proper typed defaults.

---

## When NOT to use URL state

| Anti-pattern | Why not |
|---|---|
| Form input drafts | Don't expose half-typed values in the URL |
| Sensitive filter values | Avoid PII in URLs (logged, cached, leaked via referrer) |
| High-frequency local state (e.g. mouse position, scroll) | Would cause excessive history pollution |
| Toggle that should reset on navigation | Use local state — that's what makes it "ephemeral" |

---

## Server Components and URL state

Server Components can read `searchParams` directly without a hook:

```tsx
// app/(app)/resources/page.tsx (Server Component)
type Props = {
  searchParams: Promise<{ tab?: string; filter?: string }>
}

export default async function Page({ searchParams }: Props) {
  const params = await searchParams
  const tab = params.tab ?? "list"

  return <ResourceListScreen initialTab={tab} />
}
```

The client component then takes over with `useSearchParams()`.

---

## Constraints

- Tab / filter / sort / page state lives in the URL, not `useState`
- Encapsulate per-screen URL state in `_hooks/use{Feature}UrlState.ts`
- Validate untrusted URL input with Zod
- Reset pagination to page 1 whenever a filter or sort changes
- Use `router.push` (history) by default; `router.replace` only for quiet/debounced updates
- Never put form draft values or PII in the URL
